Practical Restoration Guidance

Clothing & Textile Restoration FAQs

Straightforward answers about fire, smoke, soot, water and flood-affected clothing and textiles. Every item requires an individual assessment.

Fire & Smoke DamageWater, Flood & Mold DamageClothing & Household TextilesInsurance Claims & CostsRestoration Process & TimingService Area, Free Pickup & Contact

Fire & Smoke Damage

Can clothing be restored after a house fire?

Many garments affected by fire, smoke or soot can be restored. Fabric type, heat exposure and contamination determine what is practical. ACR can assess the affected items.

Can you remove smoke smells from clothing?

Professional treatments may reduce trapped smoke odors in fabrics. Results vary with the material and degree of exposure; complete odor removal cannot be guaranteed.

Can soot and smoke stains be removed from clothes?

Some soot deposits and smoke-related stains can be treated. Avoid rubbing soot into fabrics or using household stain removers before an assessment.

What should I do with my clothes immediately after a fire?

Enter only when officials say it is safe. Photograph affected belongings and avoid unnecessary handling, washing or spraying soot-covered garments. Contact ACR for guidance.

Water, Flood & Mold Damage

Can clothes damaged by flooding or a burst pipe be saved?

Many water-damaged garments and household textiles may be recoverable. The water source, time exposed and contamination affect the outcome.

Can you restore clothing with mold or mildew damage?

Some affected textiles may qualify for restoration after assessment. Severely contaminated items may be unsuitable for cleaning or reuse.

How quickly should water-damaged clothing be treated?

Seek guidance as soon as it is safe. Prolonged dampness can worsen staining, odors and microbial growth. Avoid handling items exposed to sewage without appropriate precautions.

Clothing & Household Textiles

What types of clothing can ACR restore?

Shirts, trousers, suits, dresses, coats, uniforms and other garments may be evaluated individually. Each item's condition determines the treatment.

Can wedding dresses and sentimental clothing be restored?

Wedding gowns, family keepsakes and delicate garments may be candidates for specialized care. View original ACR restoration photographs to see examples, not guarantees.

Can you restore comforters, blankets, curtains and bedding?

Bedding, comforters, quilts, blankets and drapery may be assessed for restoration after smoke, fire or water exposure.

Can delicate fabrics such as silk and wool be restored?

Silk, wool, lace and embellished fabrics need special evaluation because dyes, finishes and fibers may respond differently to treatments.

Insurance Claims & Costs

Does homeowners insurance cover clothing damaged by fire or water?

Many policies cover personal belongings after qualifying losses. Coverage, deductibles and exclusions vary. Ask your insurer or adjuster about your specific claim.

Can ACR work with my insurance adjuster or restoration contractor?

Contact ACR to discuss coordinating textile restoration with your insurance adjuster or property restoration contractor and any needed documentation.

Is restoring damaged clothing cheaper than replacing it?

Restoration can cost less than replacement for some losses, depending on the items, damage, cleaning requirements and replacement value. Each job needs assessment.

What happens when an item cannot be restored?

Heat damage, deterioration or contamination may prevent restoration. Ask ACR about documenting the condition for any insurance-related next steps.

Restoration Process & Timing

How does the clothing restoration process work?

The process generally involves assessment, sorting, suitable cleaning or odor treatment, drying and inspection. Treatments depend on the condition of each item.

How long does clothing restoration take?

The timeframe depends on the number of items, fabric types and damage severity. ACR is available 24/7 for inquiries; this does not mean every restoration can be completed immediately.

Will my clothing look and smell exactly as it did before?

ACR aims to recover items when practical, but permanent discoloration, fiber damage or contamination can limit results. No outcome is guaranteed.

Service Area, Free Pickup & Contact

Which counties and communities can ACR serve?

ACR is based in Ephrata and accepts inquiries from listed communities across the region, including outside Pennsylvania. Its estimated travel limit is 120 minutes (2 hours); confirm free pickup for your address. See the Service Areas directory.

How do I get started, and do you offer 24/7 help and free pickup?

Yes. ACR is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for inquiries and offers free pickup. Contact ACR to describe the damage and arrange free pickup.
